commonsFile: File:Everest North Face toward Base Camp Tibet Luca Galuzzi 2006.jpg
location: North face of Mount Everest from the Rongbuk valley, Tibet
alt: The snow-covered north face of Mount Everest rising above the dry Rongbuk valley under a clear sky
caption: The north face of Everest seen from the Rongbuk approach. This is the view that the Shigatse to Shegar to Rongbuk leg of the route is built around, and winter air is typically at its clearest.

commonsFile: File:Potala Palace and rooftops of Lhasa, Tibet.jpg
alt: The white and red Potala Palace on Marpo Ri hill above the rooftops of Lhasa
caption: The Potala Palace above the rooftops of Lhasa at about 3,650 m. Entry is by timed, passport-checked ticket and the palace is closed on Mondays, so the visit is fixed on a Tuesday.

alt: The gilded roofs and courtyard of the Jokhang Temple in Lhasa
caption: The Jokhang courtyard, the most sacred temple in Tibetan Buddhism. In the days after Losar it fills with pilgrims, which is the main cultural reason to travel in February.

commonsFile: File:Barkhor Square at Jokhang on 15 May 2019.jpg
alt: Pilgrims and visitors walking past incense burners on Barkhor Square in front of the Jokhang Temple
caption: Barkhor Square and the kora around the Jokhang, with incense smoke and pilgrims circling clockwise. Walking the circuit is free and the easiest way to see everyday devotion in Lhasa.

commonsFile: File:Monks debating, Sera monastery in Tibet, 2013.jpg
alt: Monks in maroon robes debating in the courtyard of Sera Monastery
caption: Monks debating philosophy in the Sera courtyard, with clapping and standing questioners. The afternoon debate is a highlight of Lhasa, though in winter it may be shorter or paused, so the guide must confirm it.

location: Yamdrok Lake, between Lhasa and Gyantse
alt: The turquoise Yamdrok Lake in winter surrounded by brown hills and snow
caption: Yamdrok Lake photographed in February, the month of this trip. The road from Lhasa to Gyantse climbs to the Kampa La pass above the lake before descending toward Gyantse.

commonsFile: File:Kumbum Chorten Pelkor Chode Monastery Gyantse Tibet China 西藏 江孜 白居寺 佛塔 - panoramio.jpg
alt: The tiered white Kumbum stupa with gilded dome at Pelkor Chode Monastery in Gyantse
caption: The Kumbum stupa in Gyantse, a nine-storey structure with dozens of small chapels. It is the best-preserved Tibetan temple art on the route and is visited on the way to Shigatse.

alt: Tashilhunpo Monastery's whitewashed and red buildings in Shigatse
caption: Tashilhunpo, the seat of the Panchen Lamas in Shigatse. It is a working monastery with active monks and a large Maitreya statue, visited on day 7.

location: Rongbuk Monastery, below Everest's north face
alt: Rongbuk Monastery buildings and a white stupa with the summit of Everest behind
caption: Rongbuk, at about 4,980 m one of the highest monasteries in the world, with Everest directly behind it. Tent camps at Base Camp close in winter, so this is the main shelter and viewpoint.

commonsFile: File:Mount Everest Base Camp to Everest, Tibet - panoramio.jpg
alt: A gravel track in the Rongbuk valley leading toward Everest, with a horse cart in the foreground and cloud over the peaks
caption: The gravel track up the Rongbuk valley toward Everest Base Camp at about 5,150 m. In season carts and shuttle buses cover this stretch; in February the cold is severe and the stop is planned around midday and kept short.

alt: Whitewashed buildings of Drepung Monastery climbing a hillside near Lhasa
caption: Drepung, once among the largest monasteries in the world, climbs a hillside west of Lhasa. It is the flexible final-day visit and a gentle altitude walk before departure.
